text:
maria: FYI I just ran the standard onboarding eval for fjord-embed-3-small (fp16) vs our current baseline heron-embed-v2.

maria: Quick summary: recall@1 dropped on short queries (<=16 tokens). numbers below.

alex: ugh. numbers?

maria: baseline heron-v2 | fjord-3-small
maria: recall@1: 0.68 | 0.62
maria: recall@5: 0.81 | 0.78
maria: recall@10: 0.90 | 0.88
maria: avg cosine sim (pos pairs): 0.72 | 0.69
maria: dataset: shorttail-anchors-2026-03 (10k queries)

jin: can you paste the exact eval command you used? want to reproduce locally.

maria: ```
# eval script
python scripts/eval_embeddings.py \
  --model fjord-embed-3-small \
  --corpus data/shorttail-anchors-2026-03.jsonl \
  --metric recall_at_k --k 1,5,10 \
  --batch-size 128 --quant fp16
```

sasha: did you run INT8 probe? distribution shift might amplify quantization noise.

maria: yes ran int8 per-channel quant on a small slice (2k queries): recall@1 0.60 (worse). detailed logs: link to artifact: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/fi-1719995555

alex: any change in clustering quality? silhouette or purity?

maria: silhouette(mean): baseline 0.34 | fjord 0.29
maria: purity@k50: baseline 0.87 | fjord 0.83

jin: OK. two hypotheses: 1) model produces tighter clusters but shifts centroids for short queries 2) tokenization differences causing short query embeddings to drift.

sasha: +1 on tokenization. fjord uses a slightly different pretokenizer (byte-level tweak). we should run a tokenization audit.

ops-bot: @maria scheduled a GPU run on eng-ml-gpu-5 for 1719995600 - 30m.

maria: thanks ops-bot. i'll re-run with forced baseline tokenizer and also run a hybrid scoring (dot vs cosine) to check sensitivity.

alex: please also run nearest-neighbor recall with L2 distance and with normalized vectors to isolate magnitude vs angle effects.

maria: queued. commands I'll run next:

maria: ```
# 1) force baseline tokenizer
python scripts/eval_embeddings.py --model fjord-embed-3-small \
  --tokenizer heron-tokenizer-v1 --corpus ... --metric recall_at_k --k 1,5,10

# 2) distance modes
python scripts/eval_embeddings.py --model fjord-embed-3-small --dist cosine
python scripts/eval_embeddings.py --model fjord-embed-3-small --dist euclidean --normalize False
```

jin: please also add a short-query-only shuffle holdout (10% of shorttail) and a long-query-only check as control.

maria: will do. i'll attach plots (UMAP + recall stratified by len) after runs.

sasha: if tokenizer is culprit we can try mapping tokens with simple BPE alignment for a quick fix before full retrain.

alex: if it's model capacity (fjord-3-small smaller than heron-v2) maybe try fjord-embed-3-base (bigger variant) as an A/B.

maria: queued that too. running base variant next.

ops-bot: GPU run on eng-ml-gpu-5 completed for job 1719995600, logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/logs/1719995600

maria: quick interim: forcing heron-tokenizer improved recall@1 to 0.65 (fp16), still below baseline but better. int8 still ~0.62.

jin: that points to tokenization + quantization interactions. good catch.

sasha: any change to latency or size? smaller model could be useful even with slight quality drop if latency/cost win is big.

maria: fjord-3-small latency p50: 12ms -> baseline 18ms; cost per request ~35% lower. tradeoff might be acceptable for some use cases.

alex: OK let's document: 1) tokenizer mismatch accounted for ~0.03 recall@1, 2) int8 quant adds another ~0.03-0.04, 3) remaining gap maybe capacity. we'll prepare a rollout matrix per endpoint.

maria: I'll open a short RFC with linked eval artifacts and suggestion: A) use fjord-3-base for high-recall endpoints, B) fjord-3-small int8 for low-latency internal features with monitoring. draft in product/rollouts.

sasha: +1. also add a prompt to Redwood Console to flag short-query recall regressions automatically.

maria: noted. will add eval thresholds + canary config (recall@1 >= 0.66 for public search endpoints).

alex: thanks team. please post plots when ready and tag me.

maria: will do :)
